To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the entorhinohippocampal system is composed of two complementary subsystems: (a) a long-distance path-integration system, which is located outside the hippocampus and generates grid cell activity in dMEC and (b) a hippocampal loop, which is responsible for the emergence of "transition cells."

grid cell activity results from a path integration process located outside the hippocampus, and that the hippocampic loop allows the merging of grid cell activity with visual place cells to generate a robust place code.

the grid cell pattern can emerge from a path integration system located extra hippocampally, that the hippocampally generated "transition cells" are merged with the grid cells to provide a robust place cell activity, and that this place cell activity is merged with the path integration system to provide an efficient feedback about current location.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of the grid cells from path integration and the emergence of hippocampal place cells from the integration of grid cells and visual place cells.
the generation of grid cell and place cell activity from multimodal sensory input.
the question of how the brain builds a representation of space, and how this representation could be used to support navigation and memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

grid cell activity in dMEC results from the operation on a long-distance path-integration system located outside the HC, and that place cell activity in CA1 results from the merging of grid cell activity and visual information in the DG and EC, and the operation of a short-time path integration system in the subicula.
grid cell activity is a result of the integration of multimodal information in the EC.
the hippocampally based system provides a high-resolution positional code that is robust to the loss of the visual information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
grid cells and place cells are not two different cell types but rather two different modes of operation of the same cells.
a grid cell pattern is generated from the integration of afferent information by the EC, while a place cell pattern is built from the merging of grid cells and visual information.
the entorhino-hippocampo-parieto-retrosplenial loop is a complex and robust spatial code generator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grid cells and place cells may be generated by different mechanisms and are not necessarily linked to the same structures.
the entorhino-hippocampal loop is not a mere feedback loop but a key element for the emergence of a precise positional code.
the hippocampi of mammals are part of a larger system for spatial representation, in which they play a crucial role but not the only one.
